Google Cloud and Mysten Labs Partner to Build "Verifiable Agent Arbiter" for Verifying AI Agent Actions Onchain Mysten Labs, the developer behind the Sui blockchain, announced a joint development initiative with Google Cloud to build the "Verifiable Agent Arbiter" (VAA), an infrastructure framework designed to cryptographically verify that AI agents act strictly within authorized bounds. VAA decouples private operational logs from cryptographic proofs: detailed execution prompts, outputs, and policy decisions are housed privately within customer-managed Google Cloud storage. While cryptographic integrity proofs are anchored to the Walrus storage protocol and coordinated via the Sui network. Designed to resolve B2B transaction disputes and prevent rogue prompt injections, VAA also integrates with Sui’s native "x402" payment standard, enabling autonomous agents to discover services, trigger payments, and verify settlement trails entirely onchain. — link

Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee Says ETH Purchases Will Stop at 5% of Circulating Supply, Holdings Currently Near 4.9% Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said the company will stop accumulating ETH once its holdings reach 5% of the token’s circulating supply. Bitmine currently holds 6,016,414 ETH, or roughly 4.9% of the circulating supply, and needs to purchase about 100k more tokens, which would take an estimated six to seven weeks at last week’s buying pace. Bitmine has purchased ETH weekly since launching its Ethereum treasury strategy in June 2025. According to its latest update, the company bought another $41 million worth of ETH last week and held approximately $643 million in cash and marketable securities. — link

Kalshi Asks CFTC to Approve a Never-Expiring WTI Crude Futures Contract Kalshi has filed a proposal with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for a never-expiring futures contract tied to the WTI crude benchmark, Bloomberg reported. If approved, it would be the first crude oil perpetual traded on a US-regulated platform. The CFTC has 45 days to approve or reject it. The contract is planned to trade 24 hours a day, five days a week. Kalshi’s commodity-market volume was close to $400 million as of early September. — link

Wells Fargo, America’s Fourth-Largest Bank, in Talks With Kraken Parent Payward for Crypto Trading Liquidity as Major Banks Deepen Digital Asset Involvement Wells Fargo is in talks with Kraken parent Payward over a potential deal under which Payward would supply liquidity for crypto asset trading, CoinDesk reported, citing two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The discussions are ongoing and may not result in a deal. Payward is separately in talks with BNY over a broader financial infrastructure partnership that could cover crypto products, custody, wealth management, trading and payments. The talks highlight how major banks are increasingly turning to established crypto companies to support their digital asset ambitions. — link
